report.answer_text:
On April 2, 2025, which President Donald Trump called “Liberation Day,” the U.S. announced two tiers of new import tariffs under Executive Order 14257: (whitehouse.gov)
A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. imports, effective April 5, 2025. (whitehouse.gov)
Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, scheduled for April 9, 2025. These rates would replace the 10% baseline, not stack on top of it. The announced rates included 20% for the European Union, 24% for Japan, 25% for South Korea, 26% for India, 32% for Taiwan, 34% for China, 46% for Vietnam, 49% for Cambodia, and 50% for Lesotho. (whitehouse.gov)
Canada and Mexico stayed under separate tariff rules. The new tariffs also excluded certain goods, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and energy products, as well as steel, aluminum, and autos already covered by separate sectoral tariffs. (whitehouse.gov)
These were the originally announced rates. On April 9, the administration announced a 90-day pause on most of the higher rates, effective April 10, leaving the 10% baseline in place for most partners while raising the rate on China. (everycrsreport.com)

quotes.text: The additional ad valorem duty on all imports from all trading partners shall start at 10 percent
all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent
Such rates of duty shall apply with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 5, 2025

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state a 10 percent additional ad valorem duty on all imports, applying to goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 5, 2025, which covers the claimed baseline rate and effective date, and the 'most imports' wording is a weaker version of the quoted 'all articles'.
pages.page_reason: The page states a 10 percent additional ad valorem duty on all articles imported into the U.S. applying to goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 5, 2025, with exceptions for goods already in transit, which matches the claim's 10% baseline effective April 5, 2025 on most imports (the 'all articles' wording with 'except as otherwise provided' is consistent with 'most').
